title: Activity entry
description: One action as the hub records it (contract 03, C-03.25 to C-03.29). This file is amendment A-03.2's replacement (amendments/03-2/schemas/03-activity-entry.json, itself A-03.1's file plus the passkey kinds and rules, C-03.27b) with amendment A-10.1's one addition: the kind attach.read, a served GetChatAttach read (10 C-10.14a), whose target is the chat and whose machine and chat are set. The relayed-request part generalises the portal's remote access log line {ts, email, instance, method, path, status} (web-chat-dev.worktrees/ae-int/lib/portal/access-log.js) with a principal in place of the email and hub ids in place of the instance id; targets keep ids only, as the control audit's auditTarget does (lib/server/control/index.js). No field holds body content, a secret or a query string; the optional summary is the one field that may hold words, under contract 11.

id.description: The entry id, minted before a relayed request is forwarded so it can ride X-WC-Actor.

at.description: When the hub recorded the outcome, RFC 3339 UTC. Ordering across entries is contract 07's.

machine.description: The machine the action touched (the chat's machine for a relayed request), or null for a hub-only action.

chat.description: The chat the action touched, or null.

kind.description: What happened. Relayed routes map to kinds by the table in C-03.27; the allowlist and role kinds user.allow, user.remove and user.role are C-03.27a's (amendment A-03.1); the passkey kinds passkey.add and passkey.remove are C-03.27b's (amendment A-03.2), and a passkey sign-in is auth.sign_in or auth.sign_in_refused with a credential target; attach.read is a served read of a chat's terminal attach details (10 C-10.14a, amendment A-10.1), the one recorded read beside relay.open and relay.close; the rest are hub and connector events. A closed list for round v1; a new kind is an amendment.

target.description: What the action was on. ids only.

type.description: The kind of thing acted on.

id.description: Its id when it has one: a hub id, a daemon id from the path (ask id, element id, queue item id), or a credential id (a passkey's pky_ id, never its WebAuthn credential id). Never a secret.

action.description: For control.action: the action name as the daemon's control table names it (lib/server/control/index.js), or task-stop.

method.description: For a relayed request: the HTTP method, or WS for an upgrade (as access-log.js writes it).

path.description: For a relayed request: the path without query or fragment, at most 512 characters (access-log.js).

origin.description: For a relayed request: which chat origin it arrived on.

outcome.description: accepted, refused:<code> (the hub's or the daemon's refusal word, or the HTTP status), or failed (upstream error, timeout).

status.description: For a relayed request: the HTTP status returned to the client (101 for an accepted upgrade). Absent for hub-only actions.

related.description: Another entry this one belongs with: a relay.close names its relay.open, a message.release names the message.send that queued it, a revocation's cascade names the event that caused it.

close_code.description: For relay.close: the WebSocket close code sent to the viewer (4401, 4403, 4503 as in lib/portal/ws-relay.js, or a standard code).

summary.description: At most one summary, the only field of an entry that may hold words; its sources, cap and redaction are contract 11's (C-11.12, C-11.13).

type.description: A passkey kind's target is the passkey (C-03.27b).

id.description: A sign-in whose target is a credential was a passkey assertion; the id is the passkey's (C-03.27b).

chat.description: The chat whose attach details were read.

type.description: An attach.read's target is the chat (10 C-10.14a).
An allowlist or role kind's target is the account the entry admits (C-03.27a).
